sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year, from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $216 billion in FY2026 [F211][F1][F10].
Growth came in steps: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 [D130], was flat in FY2023 as operating income fell 57.9% [D284][D285], then rose 125.9% in FY2024 [D338].
The FY2023 trough reflected $2.17 billion of inventory provisions on Ampere Gaming and Data Center products, cutting gross margin to 56.9% from 64.9% [P35][P38][F27][F26].
FY2024 was driven by Data Center, which the filing says grew 217% [P25] and reached 78.0% of revenue [D614].

Data Center product revenue supplied 60.2pp of FY2026's 65.5% growth [D622][D448], split into 46.1pp from compute and 14.1pp from networking [D629][D636]; the product lines overlap, so they are not summed [R2].
The filing credits Blackwell demand for 59% computing growth and NVLink and Ethernet and InfiniBand ramps for 142% networking growth [P8].
Operating expenses rose 40.7% against 65.5% revenue growth [D468][D448], so incremental margin was 57.3% [D475], below the 60.4% operating margin [F50].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% against 64.7% for net income [D452][D450], helped by a 1.2% lower diluted share count [D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% [F50], against a window median of 32.8% [D813] and a low of 15.7% in FY2023 [D811].
The FY2026 bridge shows a 3.9pp drag from cost of revenue [D477], offset by 1.3pp from R&D [D478] and 0.6pp from SG&A [D479].

The largest move, FY2024's 38.5pp rise [D353], included 15.8pp from gross margin [D367], which the filing ties to Data Center growth and lower inventory provisions [P20], and 13.0pp from R&D [D368]; 5.0pp [D370] is unexplained.
Net margin trailed operating margin by 4.8pp [F50][F70] as the tax rate rose to 15.1% [D434] on fewer stock-compensation and research-credit benefits [P2].
Operating cash flow was 0.86x net income [D435] and free cash flow 0.81x [D436], the window low [D826], against a typical 0.83x [D828].
Free cash flow margin was 44.8% [D432], near the 44.4% median [D822]; capex was 2.8% of revenue [D431] and 2.13x D&A [D437].
FY2023's conversion dip came from lower net income adjusted for non-cash items, including the Arm termination cost, and higher tax payments, with operating cash flow down 38.1% [P29][D289].
Working capital likely drags FY2026, with inventory up 112.3% [D474] and receivables up 66.8% [D473], though no FY2026 passage explains either.
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion [D441] from $34.7 billion [D386].
The FY2026 cash line omits short-term investments that the pack does not carry, so that decline is overstated and the 83rd-percentile net-cash rank [D844] should not be used.
The current ratio of 3.91x [F190] sits below the 4.61x window median [D831], near the 3.52x low of FY2023 [D829].
Return on average equity of 101.5% [D447] ranks at the 100th percentile of six semis peers [D848] against a 20.3% peer median [D849].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion [D443] used 42.5% of free cash flow [D444], diluted shares still fell 1.2% [D470], and no debt was repaid [X179].
Other income rose to $11.1 billion [X120] from $2.57 billion [X119], driven by unrealized gains on equity holdings including Intel stock [P3].
These gains are non-operating, so cash conversion of 0.86x [D435] is a better earnings check than the 55.6% net margin [F70].
Two direct customers were 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue, both in Compute & Networking [P6].
Few buyers means order timing can swing revenue sharply.
Inventory rose 112.3% to $21.4 billion [D474][X222] and days inventory reached 125 [D446], up from 113 [D391] after $2.17 billion of FY2023 provisions [P35].
No FY2026 passage explains the build, and the company warns that faster product transitions can raise inventory provisions [P26].
A gross margin below 71.1% [F30] in the FY2027 10-K would extend the 3.9pp fall [D462]; recovery toward 75.0% [F29] would point to a one-off.
Free cash flow to net income below the 0.81x window low [D826] in the FY2027 10-K would show working-capital drag persisting; 0.83x [D828] would point to timing.
Days inventory above 125 [D446] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the build continues; a fall toward FY2022's 101 days [D229] would show it reversing.
